One level of a folder inside the allowed roots: folders first, then files, each in natural name order;
hidden (dot) entries and symlinks leading outside the roots are left out; at most `files.listing_cap` entries,
with `truncated` set when there were more. Every subfolder is considered, but only ten times

truncated, and its files are the first, in natural order, of those. Give `root` (its folder), `path`, or both

file system does not answer. A folder read: four are made at once (with Find Matching Files, Find Indices and
the run forms' validation and creation), the others wait for a turn, a request whose client has gone stops
waiting, and while 16 already wait the answer is a 503 with `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Create one LaueGo run from the create form's values and submit it: validated as
`validateIndexingRun` validates them (a 422 problem with every issue when one is an error; warnings do not stop
it), created (inputs resolved and published) and enqueued on its target (`local`: the portal's worker; `aps`,
`crux`: DM). A 201 with the run and its job once the run exists, also when its publication or queueing failed
(`failure` says why; the job is then Failed, or left for the remote poller when DM's reply was lost). The same
`Idempotency-Key` with the same body answers the same 201 again (24 hours); with another body, or while the first
request runs, a 409 (another body after the run was created: the 409, of type
`urn:laueportal:problem:key-created`, names it and carries its answer, `created`). A 503
`urn:laueportal:problem:not-responding` (with `Retry-After`) when the output folder's file system does not answer
run creation's own check of it, before anything is created. A folder read (it lists the input folder): four at
once with the file browser's listings, Find Matching Files, Find Indices and the validation; while 16 wait, a 503
with `Retry-After` before the key is claimed (send it again).

Needs the header `X-Laue-Portal: 1`, as every request that changes data (the portal's pages send it; scripts must too). Without it, or from a page on another origin (a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin` or `none`), the answer is a 403 problem and nothing changes.

post.description:
Start a live session: validated as `validateLiveRuns` validates it (a 422 problem with
every issue when one is an error), then, while no live run is Queued or Running (else a 409
`urn:laueportal:problem:live-session-open` naming the oldest, `open_run`), its runs are created (a live wire run,
a live LaueGo run on the folder's raw frames, or both, the LaueGo run following the wire run) and queued
together, all under one lock: two Starts never make two sessions, and the dispatcher never takes a wire run
before its follower is queued. A 201 with the runs and their jobs once they exist (`failure` on a run that could
not be created, published or queued: then none was queued). The same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body
answers the same 201 again (24 hours); with another body, or while the first request runs, a 409 (another body
after the session was started: `urn:laueportal:problem:key-created`, with `created`). A 503 with `Retry-After`,
nothing created and the key released, when DM does not answer the DAQ bind check
(`urn:laueportal:problem:dm-unavailable`) or the DAQ's folders do not (`urn:laueportal:problem:not-responding`),
and before the key is claimed while 16 folder reads wait. A folder or file of the form whose file system does not
answer the validation is an issue `not_responding` on its field, so a 422 that names it (as a batch create's
validation); one that stops answering between the validation and the run's creation is a 503 `not-responding`
that keeps the key claimed, as a batch create's. Stop a session with `cancelJob` on its first run (a follower
drains once its wire run has ended). 404 while live processing is off.

Needs the header `X-Laue-Portal: 1`, as every request that changes data (the portal's pages send it; scripts must too). Without it, or from a page on another origin (a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin` or `none`), the answer is a 403 problem and nothing changes.

post.description:
Create one wire run from the create form's values and submit it: validated as
`validateReconstructionRun` validates them (a 422 problem with every issue when one is an error; warnings do not
stop it), created (inputs resolved and published) and enqueued on its target (`local`: the portal's worker;
`aps`, `crux`: DM). A 201 with the run and its job once the run exists, also when its publication or queueing
failed (`failure` says why; the job is then Failed, or left for the remote poller when DM's reply was lost). The
same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body answers the same 201 again (24 hours); with another body, or while the
first request runs, a 409 (another body after the run was created: the 409, of type
`urn:laueportal:problem:key-created`, names it and carries its answer, `created`). A 503
`urn:laueportal:problem:not-responding` (with `Retry-After`) when the output folder's file system does not
answer run creation's own check of it, before anything is created. A folder read (it lists the input folder):
four at once with the file browser's listings, Find Matching Files, Find Indices and the validation; while 16
wait, a 503 with `Retry-After` before the key is claimed (send it again).

Needs the header `X-Laue-Portal: 1`, as every request that changes data (the portal's pages send it; scripts must too). Without it, or from a page on another origin (a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin` or `none`), the answer is a 403 problem and nothing changes.

get.description:
A complete point's depth frame (the Depth View) as stored, as the API sends frames:
`uint16`, or `float32` for a float type or values outside 0 to 65535; headers `X-Frame-Shape: H,W`,
`X-Frame-Dtype` and `X-Depth-Um` (its depth in µm). Revalidated by its `ETag`, which holds the point file's
identity: a finished point's never changes, and a point rewritten while the run writes gets another. 404 for a
depth index past the point's last, an unknown run or point, a run without a reconstruction, or a point file not
on this host (a remote run's without a portal path, or one outside the file roots: the detail says why, and
nothing is opened); 409 for a point without images (its explanation) or one that cannot be read. Six frames are
read at once: the others wait for a turn, a request whose client has gone stops waiting, and while 34 already
wait the answer is a 503 with `Retry-After`; a 503 `urn:laueportal:problem:not-responding` (with `Retry-After`)
when the run directory's or the point file's file system does not answer.

One trace per square ROI of a complete point, in the request's order, against the depth (µm) and the depth
index, as lauelab's `plot_roi_traces` plots them: the sum of the ROI's stored pixels at each depth, or with
`normalize` that divided by its own maximum (a trace whose maximum is not positive has no values, and the
reason). Each square is centred as near as it can be to `x`, `y`: never clipped or
shifted, so one that would extend outside the image is a 422 naming it (`["rois", i]`), and nothing is read. At
most 32 ROIs. Each ROI's trace is kept: those not computed yet are computed together, in one pass over the
point's frames, which waits for a turn, as the trace. Reads only. Otherwise the frames' errors.

post.description:
Index a scan log and stage it for the import: every scan of the log, in log order,
with its status (`new`, `exists`, `duplicate` or `invalid`) and the token of the staged copy
(`POST /api/v1/scans/import`; it expires 24 hours after its last use).

The log is either uploaded (`file`) or a file on the server (`path`, with `root` optionally; the path picker's
browse source): one of the two. Its size is checked against `files.max_scan_log_mb` before it is read: an
upload over it is a 413 (a 411 without a Content-Length), a server file over it a 422. The XML namespace is
`beamline.scan_log_namespace`. 400 for a path outside the roots (or outside `root`), 404 for a missing file, 422
for no source or both, a file of another type or extension (`files.scan_log_extensions`), a log with a DTD
(`<!DOCTYPE`: refused, so no entity is expanded or fetched), one that is not well-formed XML, or one with no
scan; 503 `urn:laueportal:problem:not-responding` when the server file's file system does not answer.

Needs the header `X-Laue-Portal: 1`, as every request that changes data (the portal's pages send it; scripts must too). Without it, or from a page on another origin (a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin` or `none`), the answer is a 403 problem and nothing changes.

Return the shared check immediately; refresh at most once every five minutes, with failure backoff.
Checks run on the configured launcher host, never submitting a task or allocating PBS resources.

Database (and its path), API version, the worker and its threads, the queue's counts (the job and conversion

is down: it reports `error`, and what needs it is null.
